correctness.rationale: The affine chart Z=1 is nonsingular because the derivative of y^q-g(x^p)-x with respect to x is -1. At infinity the leading coefficient forces P=[0:1:0] as sole point. In Y=1 coordinates, h=z^(d-q)-G(x,z) consists solely of p-th powers, so f_x=-z^(d-1), f_z=-(d-1)x z^(d-2). In R=k[[x,z]]/(h), z is a nonzerodivisor because h(x,0)=-a_m x^d !=0. The short exact sequence R/(z^(d-2) m) over R/(z^(d-2)) has extra k length one, giving 1+d(d-2)=(d-1)^2. Independent exact finite-field Groebner calculations for p=2 and p=3 with d=6 yielded length 25, supporting the unrestricted regular-sequence proof.
